title: FeKAN: Efficient Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks Accelerator Using FeFET-based CAM and LUT
problem: Existing in-memory accelerators optimized for MLP-based DNNs are inefficient for the dynamic B-spline basis activation (BBA) operations required by Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs), which rely on recursive B-spline interpolation rather than simple vector-matrix multiplication.
motivation: KANs are emerging as a more adaptive alternative to MLPs for complex dependencies, but their computational requirements differ fundamentally from traditional DNNs, requiring specialized acceleration.
method: FeKAN uses a software-hardware co-design approach that pre-computes the B-spline basis functions KAN needs and stores them in specialized FeFET-based memory structures (lookup tables and content-addressable memory that quickly find stored values), converting expensive dynamic calculations into simple static lookups. The system compresses the stored basis functions using sparse-data encoding, groups operations together to reduce memory traffic and power use, and optimizes the processing pipeline to prevent bottlenecks.
key_novelty: FeKAN achieves hardware acceleration specialized for KAN by using FeFET-based lookup tables and content-addressable memory to pre-compute B-spline interpolations, eliminating the need for expensive dynamic calculations.
contributions: Software-hardware co-optimized framework converting B-spline interpolation to static codebook lookups using FeFET-based LUT and CAM
Compress-sparsity-column (CSC) encoding and grouped-computation strategy for memory and energy optimization
Grouped-pipeline optimization to reduce data dependency bottlenecks
Demonstrates 150.68K-fold speedup over CPU and 4664-fold over A6000 GPU with 11196x energy efficiency improvement
limitations: Abstract does not discuss limitations such as scalability to larger models, power dissipation absolute values, or area constraints.
primary_theme: Specialized KAN accelerator using FeFET-based lookup tables
